title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (abstract page)
note: Abstract page, submitted 5 Oct 2026, v1. Headline: across three load datasets Chronos-2 is best zero-shot and fine-tuned when future covariates are available or accurate, and degrades as covariate forecasts get noisier, where TimesNet is more robust. The fetched page lists no code or data link.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (full text)
note: Design: day-ahead hourly load, 4 trained models (DLinear, PatchTST, Informer, TimesNet) and 4 pretrained (TimesFM 2.5, Chronos-2, Moirai 2.0, TiRex). Data: ISO-NE 2015-2019, an anonymous North American utility 1987-1991, CAISO 2021-2025 (gridstatus load, ERA5 temperature). Split about 3.5 y train, 6 months validation, 1 year test. Metrics MAE and MAPE, no intervals.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (full text)
note: Covariate noise is synthetic: independent zero-mean Gaussian noise added to the true future covariates, scaled by lambda (0, 0.5, 1, 5) times the validation residual spread of an ARIMA fit per covariate. No archived weather forecasts. ISO-NE also feeds the operator's day-ahead demand forecast as a covariate, left noise-free. Authors note real forecast errors are correlated and biased.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (full text)
note: Table IV, no future covariates. MAPE zero-shot/fine-tuned Chronos-2: ISO-NE 3.44/3.23, NAU 2.86/2.69, CAISO 2.72/2.55; next best Moirai 2.0 at 3.52, 3.06, 2.85; TimesNet 4.02, 3.14, 3.08. Chronos-2 gets past covariates here; the other three pretrained models are univariate. Pretrained models' context length was picked by lowest error; trained models use 168 h.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (full text)
note: Table V, future covariates; only Informer, TimesNet, Chronos-2. MAPE at lambda 0, TimesNet vs Chronos-2 zero-shot/fine-tuned: ISO-NE 1.91 vs 1.92/1.67; NAU 2.24 vs 2.31/1.99; CAISO 2.40 vs 2.47/2.13. With exact covariates zero-shot Chronos-2 is slightly behind TimesNet on all three; only the fine-tuned model leads. Fine-tuned also leads at lambda 0.5.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (full text)
note: Table V, noisy covariates. MAPE at lambda 1, TimesNet vs Chronos-2 zero-shot/fine-tuned: ISO-NE 2.19 vs 2.80/2.46; NAU 2.47 vs 2.62/2.58; CAISO 2.50 vs 3.25/2.60. At lambda 5: ISO-NE 5.17 vs 9.14/7.29; NAU 5.33 vs 5.47/5.62; CAISO 3.72 vs 5.65/3.75. TimesNet is ahead of both Chronos-2 variants from lambda 1 on every dataset.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty (full text)
note: Fine-tuning: full fine-tune of Chronos-2 only, learning rate 1e-6, batch 64, 1000 steps. All models get holiday and calendar features. Authors state the three datasets are not in the pretraining corpora as far as they know. The text names no code repository, no data release and no pre-registration; the datasets are called publicly available.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model (research source, snippets only)
note: Related study, not a replication: daily ISO-NE and ENTSO-E load, 30 to 90 day horizons, weather treated as known. Zero-shot Chronos-2 trails task-specific models; full fine-tuning brings it level or slightly ahead at 30 days. No covariate-noise test. Judged separately as chronos2-covariate-grid-load.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels (research source, snippets only)
note: Related study, not a replication: hourly load at three grid levels, 96-hour horizon, weather and holiday covariates (short-term weather forecasts for one dataset). A trained Transformer leads on two datasets and Chronos-2 on one; code, data and predictions are said to be public. No additive-noise test. Date not checked.

title: Explainable Load Forecasting with Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models (research source, snippets only)
note: Related study, not a replication: German TSO hourly load, day-ahead, ERA5 temperature and irradiance as exact future inputs. Zero-shot Chronos-2 with covariates beats a Transformer trained on one year and is slightly behind one trained on the full history. Authors call reanalysis inputs an upper bound. Code and data public.

title: RCS_time_series_forecasting_electric_load (research source, snippets only)
note: Related repository, not a replication: zero-shot Chronos-2 on hourly load for three regions, 24-hour horizon, with and without calendar and weather covariates given as actual future values. Covariates lower its error; no TimesNet and no noise test.

title: Time Series Foundation Models for Energy Load Forecasting on Consumer Hardware (research source, snippets only)
note: Related study, not a replication: ERCOT hourly load 2020-2024, several pretrained models against Prophet, SARIMA and seasonal naive under distribution shifts. No weather-covariate uncertainty experiment. Date not checked.
